title: THE GOD WHO SEES THE UNLOVED

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "When the LORD saw that Leah was not loved, he enabled her to conceive, but Rachel remained childless." - Gen 29:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
What a tender verse this is: "When the LORD saw that Leah was not loved..." God noticed. In a home where Leah was the overlooked sister, unwanted and unloved by her own husband, the Lord saw her pain — and He acted on her behalf. He gave the unloved wife the gift of children, drawing near to the very one others had pushed aside.

This tells us something wonderful about the heart of God. He has a special tenderness for the overlooked, the rejected, the second choice, the ones nobody seems to want. While the world runs after the beautiful and the favoured, God bends down to the brokenhearted. "The LORD is close to the brokenhearted" (Ps 34:18).

Perhaps you know something of Leah's ache — the feeling of being unwanted, unnoticed, or less loved than others around you. If so, hear this verse as a word straight to your heart: the Lord sees you. Your worth does not depend on whether people value you. God's eyes are upon you with compassion, and He draws especially near to those who feel unloved.

Leah did not yet have her husband's love, but she had something greater — the loving attention of Almighty God. And in time, as we will see, she would learn to find her joy not in being loved by man, but in praising the Lord who saw her.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I know the ache of feeling unloved or overlooked?
2. How does it comfort me that "the LORD saw" Leah?
3. Can I rest my worth in God's love rather than people's approval?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You see the unloved and draw near to the brokenhearted. When I feel overlooked, remind me that Your eyes are upon me with tender compassion. Amen.
